can i move an unit from one battlefield to another if I control both | RiftJudge Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Menu Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Browse / FAQ # 12774 can i move an unit from one battlefield to another if I control both verified FAQ # 12774 · asked by Rewpeskao · October 2, 2026 Answer Not with a Standard Move — a normal unit can only Standard Move Base→Battlefield or Battlefield→Base ( Rule 144.4 ); Battlefield→Battlefield requires the Ganking keyword ( Rule 810.1.b ). If the unit has Ganking, yes: exhaust it during your Main Phase in an Open State to move it from one battlefield to the other. Since you control the destination, nothing becomes Contested and no Showdown stages ( CR 452 ). Separately, card effects can move a unit battlefield→battlefield with no Ganking needed — e.g. Call to Battle, as long as the destination is a battlefield you control ( FAQ #11706 ). How does combat damage work with stunned units, and how is damage distributed among multiple blocking/attacking units? | RiftJudge Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Menu Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Browse / FAQ # 7227 How does combat damage work with stunned units, and how is damage distributed among multiple blocking/attacking units? verified FAQ # 7227 · asked by 108446050288676864 · January 4, 2026 · Rules v 1.5 · Asked before Vendetta Answer Ruling: Each player adds up the total might on their side of combat and distributes that damage to opposing units simultaneously. Stunned units do not contribute their might to their side's total. After damage is dealt, units with damage marked equal to or greater than their might are killed. Sequence: Each player totals up the might of all their units in combat (stunned units contribute 0 might) Each player distributes their total might as damage to opposing units All damage is dealt simultaneously Units with damage marked equal to or greater than their might are killed Marked damage is cleared Nuances: Damage does not reduce might When distributing damage, you must assign exactly lethal damage (damage equal to a unit's might) to a unit before you can assign damage to the next unit Each player chooses how to distribute their own side's damage among opposing units Does this answer look correct? Nuances: This applies even if you conquer a battlefield, then lose control of it (such as by using Charm to move an enemy unit there), and then reconquer it in the same turn. Can I sideboard in game 1 before the game starts? | RiftJudge Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Menu Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Browse / FAQ # 10723 Can I sideboard in game 1 before the game starts? verified FAQ # 10723 · May 28, 2026 · Asked before Vendetta Answer No, you cannot sideboard in the first game of a match. According to Rule 403.5 of the Tournament Rules: "Players may not use sideboard cards in the first game of a match." Additionally, per TR 406.1.f , the start-of-game procedure—which includes placing your Legend and Chosen Champion—occurs as part of the initial setup, and you are not permitted to use sideboard cards at this stage. Sideboarding is only permitted between games of a match ( Rule 403.4 ). Does this answer look correct? Agree 0 Disagree Comments ( 0 ) No comments yet. Log in to comment. Can you bring and reference a sideboard guide (notes made before the tournament) during a match in Riftbound? | RiftJudge Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Menu Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Browse / FAQ # 7895 Can you bring and reference a sideboard guide (notes made before the tournament) during a match in Riftbound? verified FAQ # 7895 · asked by 367700898610282498 · January 4, 2026 · Rules v 1.5 · Asked before Vendetta Answer Ruling: You can bring pre-made sideboard guides and reference them between games, but they must not be visible or accessible during individual games. Your active note-taking sheet that is visible during gameplay must start blank at the beginning of each match. Sequence: At the start of a match, any note-taking device visible during gameplay must be blank During games, pre-made notes (like sideboard guides) must be kept out of view (in a bag, deckbox, pocket, etc.) Between games, you may take out and reference your pre-made notes You can take new notes on your blank sheet during games and reference those throughout the match Nuances: There are two separate types of notes: (1) the blank sheet you write on during the current match, which can be visible at all times, and (2) pre-made materials from outside the match, which can only be accessed between games Pre-made notes can be stored in your deckbox with your sideboard without issue during deck checks, as long as they're not accessed during games Does this answer look correct? Is it legal for the top 2 players to intentionally draw during the last match of the Swiss phase in a competitive event? | RiftJudge Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Menu Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Browse / FAQ # 2764 Is it legal for the top 2 players to intentionally draw during the last match of the Swiss phase in a competitive event? verified FAQ # 2764 · asked by 140793142185033728 · January 4, 2026 · Rules v 1.5 · Asked before Vendetta Answer Ruling: Intentional draws are 100% legal at any point in a tournament, including the last match of Swiss. Players may mutually agree to draw a game or match at any time before it is completed, as long as no bribery or out-of-game incentives are involved. Nuances: Intentional draws cannot be made in exchange for anything (bribery, out-of-game rewards, or incentives) Prize sharing agreements are allowed as long as they are not offered or accepted in return for the outcome of a game or match Players are allowed to concede every game if they choose, though there is little strategic reason to do so Draws award 1 point while wins award 3 points, making strategic intentional draws only advantageous in specific situations Forcing players to play out matches when both benefit from a draw can lead to non-competitive play where both players simply pass for turns Does this answer look correct? If a match reaches 1-1 in games with only a few minutes left on the clock, do players proceed to a third game? | RiftJudge Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Menu Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Browse / FAQ # 4557 If a match reaches 1-1 in games with only a few minutes left on the clock, do players proceed to a third game? verified FAQ # 4557 · asked by 400856445916020738 · January 4, 2026 · Rules v 1.5 · Asked before Vendetta Answer Ruling: Yes, players start game 3. When time in the round is called, the match goes to turns, and whoever has the most points at the end of turns wins the game. Sequence: Start game 3 When time is called, proceed to turns Player with the most points at the end of turns wins the game Does this answer look correct? If a spell like Void Seeker has multiple instructions (deal damage to a target, then draw a card), and the target becomes illegal, does the draw still resolve? | RiftJudge Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Menu Browse Chat Ask Leaderboard Review Help Sign In Browse / FAQ # 1833 If a spell like Void Seeker has multiple instructions (deal damage to a target, then draw a card), and the target becomes illegal, does the draw still resolve? verified FAQ # 1833 · asked by 515618885576425496 · December 31, 2025 · Rules v 1.5 · Asked before Vendetta Answer Ruling: When a spell has separate instructions and the target becomes illegal, only the instruction requiring the illegal target fails to execute. Other instructions that don't require that target still resolve. Sequence: The deal damage instruction fails because the target is no longer on the battlefield The draw card instruction still resolves because it doesn't require the target Does this answer look correct?
